What a prom night costs, before tax

Published hourly rates run $145 to $325 for the vehicles on this page. A 5-hour booking comes to $1,475 before tax in the Pink Hummer Limo (18 seats), $1,250 in the Party Bus (28 Pax) (28), $875 in the Limo Lounge Party Sprinter (16) and $725 in the Executive Black Sprinter (14). Arizona sales tax of 8% goes on at checkout. Nothing else joins the total: no service charge, no fuel surcharge, no booking fee, no per-mile charge.

All the vehicles listed here carry a 4-hour minimum except the 56-Passenger Motorcoach (5-hour minimum). That is the table a prom night is quoted from, on those same minimums: there is no second price list for a school dance. A long evening also bills for less than the clock suggests, because 7+ booked hours earn 1 free hour, 12+ earn 2, 15+ earn 3, taken off the billable total — 7 hours in the Pink Hummer Limo bill as 6 hours, or $1,770 before tax.

How a prom booking works here

It is a chauffeured hourly charter across the whole evening: collect the group — house by house, or from one address everyone meets at — take the photograph or dinner stop, drop at the doors in time for the start, and run the returns inside the reserved hours. Those stops are complimentary, because the hours are already bought. Send the passenger count, the addresses in the order you want them driven and a guardian cell number, and the chauffeur works one written schedule instead of a group chat.

Which vehicle for a prom group

Count everyone who has to travel together before you compare rates. The Pink Hummer Limo seats 18 and is the arrival the photographs are built around. The party cabins carry lounge seating, sound and lighting and seat 13–28 passengers per vehicle: the Party Bus (28 Pax), Limo Lounge Party Sprinter, Limo Party Sprinter (13 Pax) and Ultra Luxury Party Sprinter. Where the group is larger than one cabin, or parents want a vehicle of their own, the shuttles and coaches seat 14–56 passengers per vehicle: the Executive Black Sprinter, Executive White Sprinter, Mini Bus (24 Pax), Grech Executive Mini Coach (27 Pax), Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) and 56-Passenger Motorcoach. Two vehicles travel on one written itinerary; send the full headcount and the stop list and the schedule is built from both.

A prom night, in the order it happens

Start times differ from school to school, so read what follows as an order rather than a clock. The sequence is the part that repeats: get everyone aboard without a scramble, leave room for photographs, arrive together, and get home on a plan the parents have already read.

House-by-house pickups, or one address the group meets at

Two ways to start the evening, and one of them costs time. A list of homes means the chauffeur works driveway by driveway, and every driveway is minutes, so the first pickup has to be earlier than anyone expects. One address where the group gathers buys those minutes back. Either is fine; what matters is that the addresses and their order are on the reservation, so the schedule is built from the real route.

Photographs or dinner before the doors open

Optional, and it sits inside the hours already reserved. A park, a desert backdrop, a family front garden, a restaurant: give us the address at booking so the chauffeur can plan where a vehicle that size might actually stop, rather than circling the block with the group aboard. Food and confetti stay outside the cabin (ride rules).

Arriving together

The reason to book one vehicle is that everybody steps out at the same moment at the same doors, instead of arriving in ones and twos out of four cars. The drop is timed to the start of the dance rather than to somewhere near it, and the pickup point for the end of the evening is written into the schedule before anyone leaves — so nobody is negotiating it by text message afterwards.

Returns inside the reserved hours

Inside the hours on the booking, students go back to the homes or the gathering address on the schedule. If the evening is going to run past the block you reserved, extend before the hours run out — same published hourly rate, subject to availability. An after-prom stop goes on the request the same way: timing, access at the address and the return plan are reviewed before the route is confirmed in writing.

An illustrative 5-hour block, an example and not a published schedule: first pickup, the remaining pickups, photographs, the drop at the doors, then the returns as written. Put your own start time against the drop and work backwards.

What a prom charter costs (published rates)

Fare = published hourly rate × billable hours, and there is no second calculation hiding behind it. No per-mile charge, no service fee, no fuel surcharge. Full rate table →

One chauffeur, one schedule, one contact

The chauffeur assigned to the evening is background and MVR checked and drug screened; the cabin is detailed between every trip — not at the end of the day; and bottled water on every ride.

The house rules on board are the ones every other trip runs on; there is no relaxed edition for a school dance. If anyone travelling is under 21, the trip is alcohol-free for the whole group, adults included:

Put a guardian cell number on the reservation. One number gives the chauffeur a single point of contact for the evening — a pickup that moves, a dance that lets out early, a change to the return. Music and lighting are welcome. The same schedule works for homecoming transportation and for a quinceañera transportation day.

  • No underage drinking. Anyone under 21 stays on soft drinks.
  • No eating or food inside the vehicle. Drinks are fine; snacks wait for the next stop.
  • No smoking or vaping of any kind. The smell does not leave, so this one carries a fee. $1,500.
  • Keep the drinks in the cups. Minor spills are fine; a can or two on the floor counts as excessive and carries a cleaning fee. $450.
  • If someone gets sick in the vehicle, we have to deep clean it, and that carries a cleaning fee. Pace yourselves. $450.
  • No heels or shoes on the seats. They are leather and they remember.
  • Take your trash with you at the end. Cans, cups, confetti, all of it.

How to book a prom charter

  1. Count everyone who has to ride together, then pick the vehicle that holds them
  2. Set the date, the first pickup time and the stop list (homes or one gathering address, photographs or dinner, the dance, the returns)
  3. Confirm online — or call/text (623) 986-6339 / email reservations@scottsdalesprinters.com
  4. Pay at checkout to hold the date

What the deposit does: How the rest settles depends on how you pay: on a card, a 50% deposit holds the date and your written confirmation sets out the balance and its timing; paying in full at checkout leaves nothing else due before your ride; a payment link from the reservations desk opens that same checkout. Availability varies by date and by vehicle. Request a current quote for your date and we confirm in writing what is open.

Have ready when you book: the passenger count, every pickup address (or the one gathering address), any photograph or dinner stop, the address of the dance, your first pickup time, the return plan, and a guardian cell number.

Live availability and checkout sit on the pricing page. To walk the schedule through with a person first, contact reservations or read the FAQ.

Frequently asked questions

How much does it cost to rent a limo for prom?

The fare is the published hourly rate times the billable hours, plus 8% Arizona sales tax at checkout. Across the vehicles on this page the rate runs $145 to $325 an hour. A 5-hour evening is $1,475 before tax in the Pink Hummer Limo, $875 in the Limo Lounge Party Sprinter and $725 in the Executive Black Sprinter. All the vehicles listed here carry a 4-hour minimum except the 56-Passenger Motorcoach (5-hour minimum).

Do your prices change for prom?

There is no prom rate card. A prom night is quoted from the same published hourly table as any other date, on the same 4-to-5-hour vehicle minimums, with no event surcharge and no per-seat price. What varies by date is availability, so reservations confirm in writing what is open before anything is paid. That table is on the pricing page, and it is the one the checkout charges from.

What does that work out to per person?

Divide the pre-tax fare by the seats. At 5 hours that is ~$82 a head in the Pink Hummer Limo (18 seats), ~$45 in the Party Bus (28 Pax) (28) and ~$29 in the 56-Passenger Motorcoach (56). It is arithmetic for splitting the bill, not a per-seat price: you reserve the vehicle, so the total is the same however many seats are filled.

How many students fit in a prom limo or party bus?

The vehicles on this page seat 13–56 passengers each, and every seat count is printed beside its rate above. The Pink Hummer Limo seats 18; the party cabins seat 13–28 per vehicle; the shuttles and coaches seat 14–56. Count the chaperones and parents riding too. A group that does not fit one cabin is quoted a second vehicle on the same written itinerary.

Is a party bus or a limo better for prom?

They are priced the same way and differ in the cabin. A limousine cabin is the arrival: the Pink Hummer Limo seats 18. A party bus takes more people in one cabin, with lounge seating down the sides — the Party Bus (28 Pax) seats 28. The Limo Lounge Party Sprinter sits between them at 16. The comparison guide sets the three formats side by side.

Can one booking cover several home pickups, a photo stop and the dance?

Yes, and it is the ordinary shape of a prom booking. On an hourly charter those stops are complimentary, because the hours are already reserved. Send every address in the order you want it driven and the whole evening goes onto one written schedule, returns included.

Is alcohol allowed on a prom charter if anyone is under 21?

No. If even one passenger is under 21 the trip is alcohol-free for the whole group, adults included — that is a house rule, not a prom rule. Give reservations the passenger ages and the guardian contact when the schedule is arranged, and it is recorded before pickup. Bottled water on every ride. The Arizona rules behind it are in the alcohol guide; the full house list is on ride rules.

How do parents stay in the loop on prom night?

Put a guardian cell number on the reservation: that number is the chauffeur’s single point of contact if the timing moves. A parent can make and manage the booking themselves. The stop list, the drop and the return plan are confirmed in writing beforehand, which is the other half of the answer — most of what a parent wants to know is settled before anyone gets in.

Can we add an after-prom stop?

Add the stop and the guardian contact to the request. Timing, access at that address and the return plan are reviewed before the route is confirmed in writing, so the answer arrives before you pay rather than at the curb. The stop sits inside the hours you reserve, like every other stop on an hourly charter.

What holds a prom date, and what if the plan changes?

Payment at checkout holds it — what you pay today and what is left depends on how you pay, which is set out above. Which cancellation window applies is worked out from your booking — the pickup date, the headcount and the vehicle count among the inputs — and this article states none of the windows; check yours before you pay. A date change is a different question — ask 72 or more hours ahead and we move the booking once, free, subject to availability, with the deposit carried over and the new date's rate applied. Complete terms, including major-event dates: policies.

Which Valley cities do you cover for prom?

We run across Scottsdale, Phoenix and the East Valley. The cities with a coverage page of their own are Scottsdale, Phoenix, Paradise Valley, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Glendale, Cave Creek and San Tan Valley. Confirm every address when you book, so the driving sits inside the hours you reserved rather than eating into the evening.
